# Timed upgrades show a timer

> **Headline:** Every HUD row with a live countdown gains a code-drawn arc ring
> around its icon that fills as a charge recharges (and drains as a timed window
> expires), so the player can read timing at a glance instead of parsing the
> `next in Ns` text.

## Problem statement

Timer-driven upgrades are readable only as **text**: a recharging consumable row
appends `next in Ns` to its label, a timed window shows `Ns` in the value column,
and an owned-but-empty pool is greyed out. Mid-combat the player must read and
parse that text to know how close the next charge (or the end of the window) is.
The upgrade's own icon — the thing the player already uses to identify the item —
carries no timing information at all.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (primary).**
  - *As a player*, while my Teleport pool is empty, I want to see **at a glance**
    how far the recharge has progressed, so I can decide whether to hold position
    or push into danger.
  - *As a player*, while a timed upgrade is running (e.g. Speed Boost), I want the
    icon to show how much of the window is left, so I do not have to read the
    seconds column while dodging.
  - *As a player*, when a charge becomes available — or a window ends — I want the
    indicator to read unambiguously without reading a number.
- **Producer/operator.** One consistent timing affordance on every countdown row,
  so the HUD never mixes "some rows have gauges, some do not".

## Existing state (verified in the repo)

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` renders one row per power-up as `[icon Graphics, label Text,
  value Text]` (weapon rows likewise via `_addWeaponRow`) and rebuilds every row
  on each `refresh()`, called per frame from `HUD.update()`. Teardown goes through
  `_rowObjects`.
- Icons are code-drawn: `drawPowerUpIcon(...)` / `drawWeaponIcon(...)` in
  `src/powerups/icons.ts`, drawn at **8 px** at `ICON_X = 10` inside a
  **`HUD_ROW_HEIGHT = 22`** row; the label column starts at `NAME_X = 24`.
- Four countdown sources exist today, and they are **not** uniform in the data
  they expose:
  1. **Consumable recharge** (`Teleport`, `Phase Shift`, `Shield`, `Thorn Field`,
     `Force Field`, `Mystery UFO`): `EffectsRegistry.consumableRechargeRemaining(id)`
     → the soonest in-flight timer. `PowerUpLevelStore._rechargeTimers` keeps
     `number[]` of **remaining seconds only** — the per-timer duration captured at
     consumption is not stored, so a fraction is not currently derivable.
  2. **Power-up timed window** (e.g. `Speed Boost`, `Salvage`):
     `powerUpTemporaryRemaining(id)`; the internal `_timed` entries already hold
     `{ duration, remaining }`.
  3. **Weapon field-pickup window**: `activeWeapons()` already returns
     `WeaponEffect { duration, remaining, tempWindow }`.
  4. **Permanent Orbital Strike cadence**: `strikeNextBoltSeconds()` plus
     `strikeInterval()`.
- The empty-pool state already exists: `HUD._isPowerUpGreyed(id)` paints icon,
  label and value with the shared `POWER_UP_GREY_COLOUR`; non-slot rows are dimmed
  via `NON_SLOT_ROW_ALPHA`.
- A proportional-fill precedent exists on the same HUD (the mineral hold bar,
  `_drawMineralBar`, with a `MINERAL_BAR_MIN_FILL` legibility floor).
- The HUD is one shared class used by `PlayScene` and every gym that shows it, so
  an indicator implemented here is game↔gym-parity correct by construction.
- No mask/clip usage exists anywhere in `src/` (`createGeometryMask` is unused),
  which is why the operator chose the mask-free arc form.

## Desired change

Every HUD row that has a **live countdown** gains a **sweeping arc ring around its
icon** — code-drawn, no mask, no external asset — that shows the fraction of that
countdown currently available:

- **Arriving** countdowns (a charge recharging, the next Orbital Strike bolt):
  the ring **fills clockwise from empty to complete** as the wait elapses; empty
  the moment the charge is spent / the bolt fires, complete when the event is due.
- **Expiring** countdowns (a timed power-up window, a weapon field-pickup window):
  the ring **drains clockwise from complete to empty** as the window burns down;
  complete at pickup, empty at expiry.
- Rows with **no live countdown** (pool full / permanent `∞` / no pending bolt) draw
  **no ring** and render exactly as today.

Ring geometry (proposed, to be tuned during implementation): centred on the row
icon, radius just outside the 8 px glyph, thin stroke (≈2 px) in the item's own
palette colour (`ICON_COLORS[id]` / weapon icon colour), swept from 12 o'clock
clockwise, with a minimum visible sweep while the timer is live so a nearly-done
countdown never flickers to invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single progress seam.** The arc fraction comes from one shared, pure
  helper (e.g. `resolveCountdownFraction({ remaining, total, mode })`) plus
  registry/store accessors; no per-kind fraction arithmetic is duplicated in the
  HUD, and the game and every gym read the same seam.
- **AC2 — Arriving countdowns fill.** For a consumable recharge and for the
  permanent Orbital Strike cadence, the rendered fraction rises monotonically from
  `0` at the spend/fire instant to `1` when the charge returns / the next bolt is
  due, and it agrees with the same timer the existing `next in Ns` label reports
  at every refresh (icon and text can never disagree).
- **AC3 — Expiring countdowns drain.** For a power-up timed window and a weapon
  field-pickup window, the fraction starts at `1` and decreases monotonically to
  `0` at expiry, derived from the window's own captured `duration`, never from a
  hard-coded TTL.
- **AC4 — No countdown, no ring.** Rows with nothing counting down (full pool,
  permanent-only `∞` row, no pending bolt, non-timer rows such as Magnet level or
  the lives row) draw no arc and are otherwise byte-identical to today's output
  (regression test).
- **AC5 — Reset on reuse.** Spending a returned charge restarts the ring from empty
  (no stale complete ring), and a refreshed/restarted window restarts from complete
  (no stale empty ring).
- **AC6 — Multiple in-flight charges.** With several charges recharging, the ring
  reflects the **soonest-returning** charge — the same timer the label reports —
  and the ` ×N` charge count is unchanged.
- **AC7 — Legibility and layout invariants.** The ring fits inside the row without
  moving the label, value, marker or budget columns; it reads at 8 px icon size;
  the state is distinguishable without relying on hue alone (arc length + the
  existing shared grey); the greyed/non-slot alpha rules are preserved.
- **AC8 — No leak.** Rebuilding the HUD each frame does not grow the scene child
  list: after many `refresh()` calls the rendered-object count is bounded
  (regression test alongside the existing teardown assertions).
- **AC9 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests for the pure fraction helper (all four
  sources, edge cases at `0`, `1`, zero/undefined totals), HUD row-model tests
  asserting the fraction each row reports, a rendering test that the arc Graphics
  carries the expected fraction, and per-state coverage for at least one kind of
  each of the four countdown sources — written to fail before the implementation.
- **AC10 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 HUD presentation
  paragraph) and the `src/ui/HUD.ts` module docblock describe the ring, its two
  directions and the "no live countdown, no ring" rule; the progress seam is
  explained in code comments.
- **AC11 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Code-first visuals:** no new art assets, no new runtime dependencies (repo
  convention for every icon and effect).
- **Mask-free:** the chosen form must not use a geometry/bitmap mask; `Graphics`
  arc drawing only (no mask precedent exists in `src/`).
- **Per-frame rebuild:** `HUD.refresh()` destroys and recreates row objects every
  frame; the arc must ride on the row's existing `Graphics` object (or be torn down
  with it) and must not add measurable per-frame churn.
- **Single clock:** recharges keep advancing only through the shared
  `EffectsRegistry.tick` → `PowerUpLevelStore.tickRecharge` path; no second timer.
- **No behaviour change:** recharge timings, caps, grey-out rules, value-column
  semantics and the `next in Ns` text stay exactly as they are.
- **Backwards-compatible store change:** adding a per-timer total to
  `_rechargeTimers` must keep `tickRecharge` / `_advanceRechargeTimers` semantics
  and their existing tests green.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — row model gains the fraction; `_addRow` / `_addWeaponRow` draw
  the ring around the row icon.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — shared ring-drawing helper (same palette, same
  8 px glyph geometry).
- `src/ui/hudCountdown.ts` *(new, or a small helper inside `icons.ts`)* — the pure
  `resolveCountdownFraction` seam.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — store per-timer total and expose
  `consumableRechargeProgress(id)`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — registry projections: consumable recharge progress,
  power-up window total (weapons already expose `duration`/`remaining`).
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 HUD presentation paragraph.

## Related work

- AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW — Consumable upgrades should not be endless (parent of the
  charge-pool model).
- AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6 — HUD charge count and regeneration countdown (shipped the
  `next in Ns` text this item complements).
- AH-0MV82I97Y007MB6M — HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows (shipped the
  greyed empty state the ring refines).
- AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP — *HUD recharge countdown indicator (recharge follow-up)*
  (open). Its text half already shipped via AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6 and this item is
  the visual half; recommendation is to close it as superseded rather than keep
  two indicators (not closed by this intake).
- AH-0MV82IAM7004KOYQ — Recharge-complete audio cue (open, **out of scope**).
- AH-0MVY3IGRC00954UD — Checkpoint does not persist consumable charge pools
  (open, **out of scope**).
- AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR — Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge.
- AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT — Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore.
- AH-0MV82I8IL0012RXY — Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence (the
  shared clock the ring reads, never a second timer).
- AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2 — Shared consumable charge pool in PowerUpLevelStore.
- AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3 — Registry one-event consumption and regeneration
  accessors (the seam the new progress projection extends).
- AH-0MVUXH3X60078QR3 — Consumable charge scene wiring and gym parity (the
  shared wiring that makes the ring game↔gym correct for free).
- AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V — Orbital Strike cadence (the `next in Ns` timer the ring
  also reflects).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 / §4.4.3 — the documented HUD presentation
  and the recharge-interval table the projection reads.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Ring vs. glyph at 8 px:** a ring just outside an 8 px glyph is roughly 9–10 px
  across inside a 22 px row. Risk: it reads as a dot rather than a gauge.
  Mitigation: tune radius/stroke during implementation and validate in the
  power-up leveling gym; if it is unreadable, escalate to the operator rather than
  silently switching form.
- **Per-frame arc churn:** one extra arc path per countdown row per frame. Mitigated
  by drawing on the row's existing `Graphics` (no new objects) and AC8.
- **Multi-charge ambiguity:** several timers can run at once; the ring shows only
  the soonest (AC6), so it must not be read as "one timer per charge". The ` ×N`
  count and the seconds label remain the disambiguators.
- **Store change blast radius:** `_rechargeTimers` becomes a richer structure;
  `tickRecharge`, `_advanceRechargeTimers`, `reset` and their tests must keep their
  current semantics.
- **Visual noise:** six rings can be on screen at once. If playtesting reads as
  clutter, the fallback is to ring only the rows whose pool is not full — a
  documented divergence to be raised with the operator, not decided silently.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the recharge-complete audio cue, checkpoint persistence of
  pools, per-charge segmented gauges, timer-balance changes and any in-world (non
  HUD) indicator are **not** part of this item; record them as linked work items
  instead of widening scope.
- **Assumption:** the value column keeps `∞`/`Ns` exactly as today; the ring is
  additive information, never a replacement.
- **Assumption:** the shared HUD is the only surface that needs the change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope: which timers drive the indicator?** *(options: (a) consumable
  recharge pools only, (b) also timed effect windows, (c) every countdown row
  including the permanent Orbital Strike next-bolt cadence)* — Answer (operator,
  interactive reply, 2026-11-03): **"(c)"** — every countdown row. Recorded in
  AC2/AC3 as the four countdown sources: consumable recharge, power-up timed
  window, weapon field-pickup window, permanent Orbital Strike cadence.
- **Q2 — Visual form** *(options: (a) icon-shaped fill through a clip/mask,
  (b) sweeping arc/ring around the icon, (c) thin bar under the icon)* — Answer
  (operator, interactive reply, 2026-11-03): **"(b)"** — a sweeping arc/ring
  around the icon. Recorded as the mask-free constraint and the ring geometry
  above. Research: `src/` contains no `createGeometryMask`, `setMask` or
  `createBitmapMask` usage, so (a) would have introduced a new rendering pattern;
  (b) needs only `Graphics` arcs.
- **Q3 — Keep the `next in Ns` text?** *(options: (a) keep, (b) remove, (c) keep but
  shorten)* — **OPEN QUESTION** (asked 2026-11-03, not answered in the round).
  Proceeding on the agent's recommended default **(a) keep**, which preserves the
  documented GDD behaviour and the several tests pinned to the label; the operator
  may switch to (b)/(c) before implementation and only the AC list changes (the
  ring work is unaffected).
- **Q — agent research, no operator input needed:** *Is a progress fraction
  available today?* — Answer (agent, repo inspection): **no** for consumable
  recharges (`PowerUpLevelStore._rechargeTimers` stores remaining seconds only);
  **yes** for power-up timed windows (`_timed` keeps `duration`), weapon windows
  (`WeaponEffect.duration`) and the strike (`strikeInterval()` +
  `strikeNextBoltSeconds()`). Evidence: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`,
  `src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts`.
- **Q — agent research, no operator input needed:** *Is this a duplicate of an
  existing item?* — Answer (agent, `wl search` over "recharge timer", "HUD icon",
  "cooldown display", "teleport charge", "power-up timer"): no **completed** item
  satisfies these ACs (the text countdown AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6 and the greyed empty
  row AH-0MV82I97Y007MB6M both shipped); the still-open AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP is a
  partial overlap recorded under Related work, with a recommendation to close it
  as superseded.

## Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (`find-related-full-AH-0MVZ8YQQV006Q09W.md`
records the untruncated report). Off-topic matches — `AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2`
(level/wave progress label) and the `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` keyword hits —
were dropped as noise.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3** – Registry one-event consumption and regeneration accessors (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXH3X60078QR3** – Consumable charge scene wiring and gym parity (completed)

## Problem

`src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` » `records the measured ring timings and their tolerance` pins the four measured ring-timing means as literals:

```
expect(spec).toMatch(/49\.2/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/109\.0/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/34\.1/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/62\.6/);
```

The GDD §8.2 table those assertions guard is a *transcription* of `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the artifact the same test already asserts is cited). So every legitimate arena recalibration requotes the artifact and the GDD together, and strands the guard until someone hand-edits four more numbers — which is exactly what happened twice:

- AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0 (ring-2 budget/measurements) — no, stale only after the wrap-aware bot landed;
- AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG (wrap-aware bot) raised the measured grind 91.6 → 109.0 min;
- AH-0MW09QIJU000DAGT (commit `a7c57da1`) recalibrated the ring-2 window to 90–120 min and regenerated the artifact, leaving the guard red until commit `032d96e9`.

The failure was caught (good), but the literals are the wrong source of truth: the guard should assert *agreement with the artifact*, not a copy of it.

## Desired change

In `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`:

1. Read `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the path the guard already requires the GDD to cite) and derive the expected one-decimal mean for each `ringIndex`/`strategy` pair (`1-grind`, `2-grind`, `1-rush`, `2-rush`) from `summary.totalMinutes.mean.toFixed(1)`.
2. Assert the GDD §8.2 prose quotes each of those four values with its unit (`<mean> min`), so the GDD can never drift from the artifact.
3. Keep the window (40–60, 90–120) and tolerance (±2 / ±3 min) assertions explicit — those are design values owned by `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` / `RING_TIMING_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, not measurements.

A working implementation was written and verified green (full suite 419 files / 9517 tests) during AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR but dropped because the sibling item landed the literal-pinning form first; the parked commit is `9467a48a` (ref `refs/wip/AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR`) if the shape is useful.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The guard's four measured-mean assertions are derived from `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`; no measured-mean literal remains in the test.
2. Editing a mean in the artifact alone (without the GDD) fails the guard; editing the GDD to a value the artifact does not hold fails the guard.
3. The window and tolerance assertions are unchanged and still pass.
4. Full project test suite passes.

# When divers are close to the player they go slow (AH-0MW0TY1AY003TDFC)

## Problem statement

Diver dives use a **fixed 2-second duration** (`DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` in `src/entities/Diver.ts`), so the entity's dive speed is inversely proportional to the distance it travels: a close-to-player dive (arc ≈ 130 px) creeps along at ≈ 65 px/s, while a full-height dive (arc ≈ 400 px) runs at ≈ 200 px/s. Because the player is usually closest when the dive is most threatening, the slowest dives occur exactly when the player is most exposed — an easy, unhurried reaction window.

## Users

- **Player:** Expects dive attacks to stay readable but to *close* at a consistent, threatening pace. A Diver that breaks off near the player is currently a non-event; it should arrive quickly.
- **Developer / designer:** Needs a single, predictable dive-speed knob so dive timing no longer varies implicitly with formation position and player location, tunable without a scene-code change.
- **QA:** Needs deterministic, testable timing that does not depend on wall-clock time or arbitrary distances.

## User stories

- As a player, when a Diver breaks formation close to me, it reaches me quickly enough that I must dodge rather than watch it drift.
- As a designer, I can tune one dive-speed value in the enemy config and know every dive (close or far) completes in the expected time.
- As a developer, I can unit-test that a dive's duration scales with its path length rather than being pinned to 2 s.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Constant dive speed (distance-proportional duration):** the Diver traverses its dive path at a fixed speed, so a dive twice as long takes twice as long to complete and a dive half as long takes half the time; no dive uses the current fixed 2-second duration.
- [ ] **AC2 — Close dives are materially faster:** with the confirmed 320 px/s dive speed, a close dive (arc ≈ 130 px) completes in ≈ 0.41 s instead of the current 2 s, a mid dive (arc ≈ 243 px) in ≈ 0.76 s and a full dive (arc ≈ 399 px) in ≈ 1.25 s — the reported "slow when close" behaviour is gone.
- [ ] **AC3 — Data-driven dive speed:** a `diveSpeed` column exists in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (diver row `320`, neutral/blank for other archetypes), is parsed into `EnemyConfig` and threaded through `enemyFactory` into `DiverConfig`, with a code default of `320` px/s when the column is absent — tuning the dive needs no scene-code change.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dive arc and lifecycle preserved:** the dive still follows the existing quadratic-bezier parabolic arc from the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start (apex at `GAME_HEIGHT * DIVER_DIVE_APEX_FRACTION`), and the FORMATION → DIVING → PAUSING → FORMATION state machine, 500 ms attack-end pause, re-anchor, facing rotation and dive SFX behave exactly as before; only the timing model changes.
- [ ] **AC5 — Test coverage:** unit tests assert the constant-speed/distance-proportional duration (e.g. two dives of different path length) and the `diveSpeed` config plumbing/default; the existing `Diver.test.ts` dive-timing helpers are updated to the new model; all affected tests pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — specifically GDD §4.1 E2 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §E2, plus the `DIVER_DIVE_SOUND_DURATION` doc comment.

## Decisions

- **Q1 — Dive speed = 320 px/s** (producer). Matches the Raider `attackSpeed` (the only existing committed-attack speed baseline) and makes close dives ≈ 0.4 s.
- **Q2 — Data-driven:** the speed is a `diveSpeed` column in `enemy-configs.csv`, parsed into `EnemyConfig`/`DiverConfig` with a code default, mirroring `attackSpeed`/`driftSpeed` and the gym enemy editor.
- **Path unchanged:** the parabolic arc shape and the pause/re-anchor/glide lifecycle are preserved; only the timing model changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared entity only:** `src/entities/Diver.ts` is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymFodderEnemies` through the shared `GymFormationScene`, so gym↔game parity is preserved by construction — no divergent copy (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **Path unchanged:** the dive remains a quadratic-bezier arc; do not alter the path shape, the pause, the re-anchor or the glide.
- **Tuning change only:** no new gameplay object.
- **Sound is a loop:** `playDiveSound` plays `aihell-diver-dive-loop` and is explicitly stopped at dive end/destruction, so a variable duration is safe; reconcile the `DIVER_DIVE_SOUND_DURATION` doc comment.
- **Fairness floor/ceiling:** a very high speed could make close dives unavoidable; 320 px/s still leaves a reaction window for a full-height dive (≈ 1.25 s).
- **CSV compatibility:** a blank `diveSpeed` for non-diver archetypes must degrade to the neutral/code default, exactly like `attackSpeed`/`commitRange`.

## Existing state

- `Diver.ts`: `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2`; `_handleDive` advances `_divePhase += dt / DIVER_DIVE_DURATION`; `computeDivePoint` evaluates a quadratic bezier at `_divePhase`.
- Measured current speeds (arc length sampled from the shipped geometry: formation start y ≈ 243, apex y = 162, player bottom y ≈ 500):

  | Dive | Arc length | Current duration | Current speed | New duration @ 320 px/s |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Full | ≈ 399 px | 2 s | ≈ 200 px/s | ≈ 1.25 s |
  | Mid | ≈ 243 px | 2 s | ≈ 121 px/s | ≈ 0.76 s |
  | Close | ≈ 131 px | 2 s | ≈ 65 px/s | ≈ 0.41 s |

- `Diver.test.ts` drives dive timing via `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION * fraction` (≈ lines 104, 485, 509, 568, 690, 705, 742, 769, 805) — these must be updated to the new model.
- `src/audio/effects.ts`: `DIVER_DIVE_SOUND_DURATION = 2` (currently an unused export; its comment references the ~2 s dive).
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` already carries per-archetype `attackSpeed`/`commitRange`, so the `diveSpeed` column follows an established pattern.

## Desired change

Replace the fixed-duration dive with a **fixed-speed, data-driven** dive:

1. Add a `diveSpeed` column to `enemy-configs.csv` (diver `320`; neutral/blank elsewhere), parse it into `EnemyConfig` with a code default of `320` px/s, and thread it through `enemyFactory` into `DiverConfig`.
2. At dive start, compute the dive path length (bezier **arc length**, numerically sampled; straight-line distance is an acceptable simpler approximation).
3. Set `duration = max(pathLength / diveSpeed, MIN_DIVE_DURATION)`.
4. Advance `_divePhase` by `dt / duration`.
5. Update tests and docs.

## Assumptions

1. The parabolic arc shape is preserved (the operator asked only to change the timing model).
2. Measuring the bezier **arc length** (not straight-line distance) is preferred so the along-path speed is genuinely constant; straight-line distance is acceptable if simplicity is preferred (the along-path speed would vary slightly with the arc bulge, far less than today).
3. A **minimum-duration floor** of ≈ 0.15 s is applied so a player overlapping the diver does not produce an instantaneous/teleport-like dive or a single-frame skip.
4. No maximum-duration clamp is added: at 320 px/s the worst-case on-screen dive is well under 2 s.
5. `medium` priority stands: gameplay-feel bug, not blocking and not a release blocker.
6. A blank `diveSpeed` for non-diver archetypes falls back to the neutral code default; the CSV column is inserted next to the other archetype-specific attack tuning (`attackSpeed`/`commitRange`).

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — add the `diveSpeed` column (diver `320`, neutral elsewhere) with a documented header comment.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `diveSpeed?: number` to the enemy config type.

- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — parse the `diveSpeed` column.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — thread `diveSpeed` into `DiverConfig`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — reconcile the `DIVER_DIVE_SOUND_DURATION` doc comment with the variable dive.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 E2 — document fixed-speed, data-driven diving.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §E2 — update the Diver behaviour description.

- **Diver rotates to face the player and dives towards them (AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX)** — introduced the diagonal quadratic-bezier dive this item retimes.
- **Diver should pause before returning (AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT)** — added the 500 ms attack-end pause.
- **Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return to current formation slot (AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB)** — earlier x-lock model, superseded by AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX.

- **Divers need SFX (AH-0MTVYC6E8005YN6F)** — the dive loop sound and its duration constant.

# Halve per-kill power-up drops and remove Extra Life from reward screens

## Problem statement

Too many power-ups — and in particular **Extra Life** — reach the player during a
run, so the 3-life start and the 5-life cap stop feeling meaningful and the
hold-full/mini-boss reward overlays are dominated by a pickup that trivialises
survivability. The operator wants the **per-kill power-up drop rate halved**, the
**asteroid Extra Life source stopped**, and **Extra Life removed from the
hold-full choice and mini-boss reward screens**, keeping it only as a rare field
pickup.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a run where lives are scarce and earned: fewer drops overall,
  no "free" lives from rocks, and reward overlays that offer real upgrades instead of
  a life top-up.
- **Game designer** — wants the supply dial in **one** shared place (`GameRules` /
  level-scaling curves) and no leftover Extra Life sources, so re-tuning needs one
  edit and no scene diverge.
- **Maintainer** — wants the reward pools to be honest: no dead Extra Life offer
  path, and docs/tests that match shipped numbers.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want at most half as many power-ups per kill as today, so each
  pickup feels earned.
- As a **player**, I want destroying asteroids to stop handing out extra lives, so
  lives come from deliberate play rather than rock-grinding.
- As a **player**, I want the hold-full and mini-boss rewards to offer upgrades
  rather than a life top-up, so the reward moment is about building the ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-kill drop rate halved:** `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_LEVEL_1`
  is `0.09` (was `0.18`) and `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_MAX_LEVEL` is `0.025`
  (was `0.05`), so `powerUpDropChance(level)` from `src/core/levelScaling.ts` is
  half its former value at **every** level of the 1–10 campaign while keeping the
  linear ramp (L10 stays ≈ 27.8 % of L1). The re-exported
  `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` (documented level-1 base) becomes `0.09`. Verified by unit
  tests on the defaults and on the curve endpoints plus an intermediate level.
- [ ] **AC2 — No double-halving of Extra Life's share:** `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT`
  stays `3` and no other drop weight changes, so Extra Life's *relative* rarity in
  the shared pool (≈ 5.2 % of power-up draws) is untouched — only the per-kill roll
  falls. Its absolute per-kill chance at L1 drops from ≈ 0.93 % to ≈ 0.47 %.
  Verified by a rules/spawner-share test.
- [ ] **AC3 — Asteroids stop dropping Extra Life:** `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`
  defaults to `0` (was `0.05`); the shared rule (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`), the
  `GameRules` key and its clamping/persistence stay in place so a designer can
  re-enable it. At the default, a fully destroyed small asteroid never spawns an
  `extra_life` pickup in `PlayScene` or in any asteroid-bearing gym. Verified by
  unit tests on the default and by a seeded kill-path test at the default chance.
- [ ] **AC4 — Extra Life removed from every reward surface:** `extra_life` is
  excluded from the hold-full choice pool (`CHOICE_POOL`), from owned
  `power-up-level`/`power-up-charge` offers and from the mini-boss reward wheel
  (wedges and the empty-owned "hold-full-style" fallback). It remains a
  **field-pickup-only** power-up: still spawned by the shared drop pool, still
  granted +1 life on collection, and still levelled by field pickups. Verified by
  tests showing no `extra_life` option in hold-full draws (over many seeded draws),
  no `extra_life` wedge for a run that owns it, and the fallback pool excluding it.
  The now-unreachable demo-bot hold-full preference for Extra Life
  (`_preferredDemoChoiceIndex`) is removed or simplified with its assertions and docs
  — no dead offer path is left behind.
- [ ] **AC5 — Persisted configs adopt the new defaults:** `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  rises to `5`, and `loadRules` resets `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1`,
  `powerUpDropChanceAtMaxLevel` and `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` to the new
  defaults for any config older than version 5 (same precedent as the v2/v3
  migrations), because `saveRules` persists the whole blob and a stored
  `0.18`/`0.05` would silently defeat the change at runtime. Blobs explicitly
  stamped version 5 keep their tuned values.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation:** unit tests cover the new defaults, the migration,
  the asteroid default-off path and the reward-surface exclusions; the existing
  repo-wide guards (`src/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`)
  are updated where the exclusion is deliberate, not weakened.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One shared source of truth:** all tuning lives in `src/core/rules.ts` /
  `src/core/levelScaling.ts`; no scene, gym or test may hard-code the new numbers.
- **Gym↔game parity** (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): the game and
  every gym must run the same code. All four surfaces already live in shared modules,
  so the change must be made there, not per scene.
- **Do not delete the asteroid rule** (operator decision Q2): keep it configurable
  with a zero default.
- Extra Life's rarity *weight*, the 5-life cap, the `lifeGain` level curve and the
  catalogue entry are unchanged.

## Existing state

Three independent sources and two reward surfaces produce Extra Life today:

1. **Per-kill shared drop pool** — `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp` rolls
   `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` (linear `0.18` at L1 → `0.05` at L10,
   AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X) and draws from the shared `WeightedRandomSpawner`
   (weights: 12 standard IDs × 4, Mystery UFO 3, **Extra Life 3**, Smart Bomb 2,
   Orbital Strike 2 → pool total 58 → Extra Life ≈ 5.2 % of power-up draws; the
   weight was raised 1 → 3 by AH-0MUNS3VAQ0023L1J).
2. **Small-asteroid roll** — `rollAsteroidExtraLife` (`src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`,
   AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S) adds an independent `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` roll
   (default `0.05`, scaled by the level drop-chance ratio) on every fully destroyed
   small asteroid, additive to the generic pool. Consumed by `PlayScene`,
   `GymFormationScene` (incl. `GymMinerals`) and `GymLevel`.
3. **Hold-full choice** — `CHOICE_POOL` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) lists
   `extra_life` as a base entry (weight 1.0×), and `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`
   offers a `power-up-level` (lifeGain 1 → 3) once Extra Life is owned. Gyms
   consume the same builder (`GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeaponLeveling`).
4. **Mini-boss reward wheel** — `openMiniBossReward` builds wedges from
   `resolvePlayerSlotState(player).ownedIds` (`buildWheelWedges`), so a run that
   permanently holds Extra Life gets an Extra Life wedge; when nothing is owned the
   reward falls back to the same three-option hold-full choice
   (`_holdFullStyleRewardOptions`).

Related runtime code: the demo bot prefers an offered Extra Life in the hold-full
auto-select (`PlayScene._preferredDemoChoiceIndex`, AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4) — that
preference becomes unreachable once Extra Life leaves the pool. `saveRules` is
called by the gym interval slider (`src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts`) with the whole
`GameRules` blob, so stored configs can carry the current chance values.

Docs carrying the current numbers: GDD §4.4 (pool weights, the 0.18 → 0.05 curve,
the asteroid 0.05 roll, the `availableWhenSlotsFull` choice behaviour), GDD §3
difficulty summary, `docs/BALANCING.md` scaling table, `README.md` (rules config
and `asteroidKillDrops` entries), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
(asteroid drop), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (`GymMinerals` row).

## Desired change

- Halve the per-kill power-up drop chance curve: L1 `0.18 → 0.09`, L10
  `0.05 → 0.025`, ramp shape preserved.
- Leave every drop weight (including Extra Life's `3`) untouched.
- Default the asteroid Extra Life roll to `0`, keeping the rule and config key.
- Exclude `extra_life` from the hold-full choice pool, its owned level-up offers and
  the mini-boss wheel/fallback — one shared, documented exclusion so the game and
  every gym drop it together; Extra Life stays a field pickup.
- Retire the now-unreachable demo-bot hold-full preference for Extra Life (and its
  tests/docs), noting that on-screen Extra Life pursuit stays (field pickups still
  exist).
- Bump the rules schema to 5 so stored configs adopt the new defaults.
- Update the docs and tests that pin the old numbers.

## Key Files

- `src/core/rules.ts` — new drop-chance and asteroid-chance defaults;
  `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5` plus the v5 migration branch in `loadRules`.
- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` — doc comments and the `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`
  re-export (no formula change).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — documented `extra_life` exclusion for the choice pool
  and the owned level-up offer builder (`buildChoiceCandidates`,
  `buildOwnedPowerUpOffer`/`buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`).
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` — exclude `extra_life` from `buildWheelWedges`
  (and from the outcome pool) for owned kinds.

discovered-from:AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T (found while running the measured gate
AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL).

## Problem

The Q3 = B measured gate for the weapon nerf (**Weapon upgrades are too
powerful** (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T)) **cannot see a weapon-output change**. The
closed-loop headless arena fires the player's shots on a fixed cadence
constant:

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` → `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS = 9`,
  `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 420`, `PLAYER_BULLET_LIFETIME = 0.75` — one bullet
  every 9 ticks regardless of the equipped weapon;
- the only import from `src/utils/weapons` in the whole `src/ai/eval/` tree
  is `import type { WeaponId }` — a **type-only** import, erased at compile
  time, so `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `AOE_RADII`,
  hit budgets and `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` can never reach the simulation.

Measured, not inferred: the post-change 100-game campaign batch is
**byte-identical** to the pre-change baseline (every per-run `recordsHash`
included), and a sensitivity probe that temporarily raised
`DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS.cannon` from 2 to 12 (six times the starting
weapon's cadence) also produced a byte-identical 3-game report. Evidence:
`docs/BALANCING.md` §"Weapon 40 % trim / flattened curve — measured
before/after gate".

## Why it matters

- Every future weapon damage/output tuning item that relies on the batch gate
  gets a guaranteed zero delta and a misleading "no effect" reading.
- The intended-experience bands (`src/data/experience-targets.json`) can never
  detect a weapon-output regression, because the metric input does not depend
  on weapon data.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary already documents the limitation
  ("the arena's auto-fire is fixed"); this item closes it deliberately rather
  than leaving it implicit.

## Goal (user story)

*As the balancing agent, I want the headless arena to fire with the equipped
weapons and their level-resolved statistics, so a weapon damage, cadence or
pattern change moves the batch metrics and the measured gate can actually
answer the question it was created for.*

## Suggested approach

1. Replace the fixed auto-fire with the shared weapon resolution: use
   `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolveWeaponPattern` from
   `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` plus `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` /
   `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` / `AOE_RADII` from
   `src/utils/weapons.ts`; spawn per-weapon projectiles (pattern count,
   offsets, lifetime, size, pierce budget, bounce, AOE radius) rather than one
   bullet down the facing vector.
2. Resolve the arena's weapon levels from the same ownership context the
   hold-full choice flow already maintains
   (`ChoiceContext.weaponLevels`), so a chosen `weapon-level` upgrade rung
   changes the arena's output exactly as it does in `Player`.
3. Keep the change inside the shared code (gym↔game parity rule,
   AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): no arena-local copy of a weapon constant.
4. Re-record a baseline: the metrics will move by design, so
   `src/data/experience-targets.json` must be re-baselined
   (`targetsVersion` bump) with GDD §2.7 updated in the **same** change.
5. Re-run the weapon-trim gate evidence
   (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T / AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL) afterwards, so the 40 % trim
   finally has a measured before/after.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The arena's player projectiles are spawned from the resolved equipped
  weapon(s) (pattern count, offsets, cadence, lifetime) rather than a fixed
  `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS` bullet, asserting that a level-resolved weapon change
  changes the arena's damage output.
- [ ] A sensitivity test proves the harness now **sees** a weapon-output change:
  the same-seed batch differs when a weapon's cadence, pattern count or AOE
  radius changes (the inverse of the AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL probe).
- [ ] Weapon levels resolved from the run's ownership context feed the arena's
  fire output, so a `weapon-level` choice is observable in the metrics.
- [ ] No duplicated weapon constant or resolver exists in `src/ai/eval/`; the
  arena consumes `src/utils/weapons.ts` / `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`.
- [ ] `src/data/experience-targets.json` is re-baselined (`targetsVersion`
  bumped) and GDD §2.7 updated in the same change.
- [ ] `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary and the weapon-trim evidence
  section are updated to state that weapon output **is** modelled.
- [ ] The full project test suite passes.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the fixed auto-fire and projectile model.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — the catalogue,
  cadence, pattern and level resolvers to consume.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — the arena behaviour and determinism tests.
- `src/data/experience-targets.json`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.7 —
  the re-baseline and narrative.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the fidelity boundary and the before/after evidence.

## Notes

- Scope note: this is deliberately **not** part of the weapon-trim epic (AC4
  scope guard) — it is a harness capability gap, not a balance change.
- Do not retune any weapon value in this item; it only makes the instrument
  capable of measuring them.

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

- **AC1 — Test coverage of all four countdown sources.** Tests cover the four sources: consumable recharge (arriving), power-up timed window (expiring), weapon field-pickup window (expiring), and permanent Orbital Strike cadence (arriving).

## Goal
Create a shared code-drawn arc ring helper in `src/powerups/icons.ts` that draws a ring around a power-up icon. No masks, no external assets — `Graphics` arc drawing only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Draws a thin arc ring centred on the icon.** Ring is placed just outside the 8 px glyph, radius ≈ 5-6 px from icon centre, stroke ≈ 2 px.
- **AC2 — Uses the item's palette colour.** Ring colour comes from `ICON_COLORS[id]` (or the weapon icon colour).
- **AC3 — Sweeps from 12 o'clock clockwise.** The arc starts at 12 o'clock and sweeps clockwise for the given fraction (0–1).

## Goal
Integrate the countdown fraction into the HUD row model and draw the arc ring around each countdown row's icon. Rows with no live countdown draw no ring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Row model includes fraction.** Each HUD row that has a countdown carries the fraction from `resolveCountdownFraction` + the relevant projection.

- **AC5 — Reset on reuse.** Spending a returned charge restarts the ring from empty; a refreshed/restarted window restarts from complete.
- **AC6 — Multiple in-flight charges.** The ring reflects the soonest-returning charge (same timer the `next in Ns` label reports).
- **AC7 — Layout invariants.** The ring fits inside the row without moving label, value, marker, or budget columns. Grey-out and non-slot alpha rules are preserved.
- **AC8 — No object leak.** After many `refresh()` calls the rendered-object count is bounded (no growing child list).

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — row model and `_addRow` / `_addWeaponRow` draw the ring
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — shared ring-drawing helper (already created)

## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (60 s, desktop headless Chromium), with the dev recorder enabled:

- \`sanitiseObject\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:93\`) 0.18 % of the measured window, \`sanitise\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:65\`) 0.15 %, \`utf8ByteLength\` (\`src/telemetry/devUpload.ts:180\`) 0.14 %, \`write\` (\`src/telemetry/sinks.ts:50\`) 0.08 %, \`deepFreeze\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:459\`) 0.16 % — **~0.7 % of the window / ~7 % of JS**.
- The same run logged a skipped run-end upload: 15.8 MiB of run telemetry exceeded the 8 MiB browser→node message cap, so the recorder was serialising a payload it then discarded.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).
- Keep redaction guarantees intact: no unredacted payload may ever reach a sink.

## Out of scope

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose telemetry exceeds the upload cap no longer pays the full serialise+redact cost before discarding (verified by a test on the size-guard seam).
2. Redaction tests still pass (no path skips redaction for a payload that is written).
3. In the same profiled demo run, the telemetry bucket share is measurably lower, with the before/after numbers recorded on this item.
4. Full project test suite passes.
data.title: Dev telemetry serialisation costs ~5 % of JS during demo runs

## Goal

Record and, if the producer authorises it, act on the **raster-side** lever that remains after AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN removed the last material per-frame `Graphics` draw submission.

**Discovered from:** AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN (mobile-tier shortfall).

## Measured situation

After AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN, a 60 s `GymPerformance` run at `--cpu-throttle 4` on the reference host (headless Chromium + SwiftShader) measures **24.3–24.6 FPS** against the ≥ 30 FPS mobile-tier bar (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md` → [Baked enemy body textures](docs/PERFORMANCE.md#baked-enemy-body-textures-ah-0mw2iryah0055wcn)). The draw-submission half is now small: main-thread JS fell 22.3 % → 15.9 % of the window and the renderer bucket 19.1 % → 12.2 %, but `native` rose to \~83 % and the frame time did not move. The whole enemy+bullet draw-submission surface is only ≈ 6.5 pp of the window, and `GymPlayer` (one Graphics, no enemies) already costs ≈ 24 ms/frame on this host.

Conclusion: the residual mobile-tier gap is **software rasterisation**, not draw submission. No further main-thread JS work can close it.

## Candidate levers (all need a producer decision — they change shipped rendering)

1. **Disable antialiasing** (`Phaser.Types.Core.GameConfig.antialias`, currently the Phaser default `true`; `src/core/gameConfig.ts` sets none). On SwiftShader, MSAA multiplies fragment work. This changes the shipped look on every platform, so it needs an explicit visual-quality decision (or a mobile-only render tier, which does not exist today).
2. **Render-scale / resolution tier** — render at a lower internal resolution on the mobile tier and upscale. Same decision class as (1).
3. **Hardware-GPU verification** — the mobile-tier bar is measured on a CPU rasteriser on this host; AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P already tracks the hardware-GPU desktop runs. A hardware-GPU mobile-tier row would say whether the bar is met on real hardware (the likely answer, since the raster half is the SwiftShader artefact).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The producer decides which lever (if any) is authorised; the decision and its rationale are recorded on this item.
2. If a rendering-quality lever is authorised: it is measured with the same harness/throttle/window on the reference host, its before/after numbers and its visual-quality impact are recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, and gym↔game parity is preserved (the setting lives in the shared game config, not per scene).
3. If hardware-GPU verification is chosen instead, record the mobile-tier result and its backend (`webgl.kind`) next to the SwiftShader row so the two are never confused.

## Out of scope

- Any further draw-submission optimisation (measured and exhausted by AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN).
- Changing the mobile target or the throttle factor.

## Problem

Parent **AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87** AC5 requires: *"The same harness under a throttled CPU profile (>= 4x slowdown) sustains >= 30 FPS with 100 enemies, and the result is recorded."* Every mobile-tier row recorded so far was taken on the **software WebGL backend** (SwiftShader), because until AH-0MW2L3JXU008I2Z8 completed the host had no usable GPU:

- baseline: 19.92 FPS at 4x throttle (`a17a953b`).
- final verification: 24.21 FPS at 4x (`d2878b60`).
- after baked enemy-body textures: 24.3-24.6 FPS (`da8aaa8f`, AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN).

The recorded verdict is *"mobile tier target missed"*, and the attribution says the residual is **software rasterisation**, not draw submission or simulation.

## Why this is now re-measurable

AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P (hardware-GPU desktop verification) confirmed the harness reaches the real GPU on both desktop hosts (`--gpu --require-hardware-webgl` -> `ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.329 (NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (0x000025A0)), NVIDIA)`). The mobile tier is the same harness with `--cpu-throttle 4`, so it can now be measured with a **real GPU plus a 4x-slowed CPU** - which is a far better proxy for a mobile browser (real GPU, slow CPU) than the software-GL rows, where the rasteriser dominated.

## Preliminary evidence (this session, 2026-11-05, unpublishable)

Headless Chromium, `--gpu --require-hardware-webgl --scene GymPerformance --cpu-throttle 4`, 30 s windows, hardware WebGL confirmed in every report:

| Run | Host load | p50 | p95 | max | Effective FPS | >33 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 18.3 | 16.7 | 50.0 | 166.7 | **37.73** | 40.9 % |
| 2 | 23.1 | 16.7 | 33.3 | 116.7 | **54.10** | 8.1 % |
| 3 | 29.8 | 33.3 | 100.0 | 233.3 | 26.43 | 52.4 % |
| 4 | 36.6 | 50.0 | 133.3 | 316.7 | 16.18 | 89.1 % |

Two conclusions, neither publishable as a row:

1. The previous shortfall is at least partly a **software-rasteriser artefact**: with a real GPU the same tree clears >= 30 FPS at load <= 23 (37.7 FPS and 54.1 FPS).
2. The spread (16.2-54.1 FPS) tracks the host load, which reached 37 during this pass (other sessions). Per `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` § *Noise floor*, a run is only comparable within one load band, so **no mobile row can be published from these numbers**.

## Goal / user story

As the producer, I want the mobile tier re-measured on hardware WebGL on a **quiet host**, so parent AC5 can be closed on a real measurement instead of a software-rasteriser floor.

## Scope

- Further optimisation (the residual draw-submission work is complete; AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN records it).
- The desktop hardware runs (AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P, complete).
- Changing the >= 30 FPS bar or the 4x throttle factor.

1. A hardware-WebGL mobile-tier run (4x CPU throttle, 100 enemies, 60 s) is recorded with `webgl.kind: "hardware"` and the driver string, at a host load inside the documented baseline band.
2. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` carries the new row(s) plus the re-stated mobile verdict, with the software-GL rows retained as the host floor.

- `src/performanceDocs.test.ts` - pinned docs assertions
- `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` - no change expected (read-only use)
